Still, the 6-1 start means the 49ers don't have to panic to trade for a fill-in. And their failed pursuit of Vikings WR Jauan Jennings , which would have been a relatively low-wattage trade, suggests they are looking for more stopgap than superstar. This is the 49ers' best remaining chance, with a 6-1 record and relatively good health, to win a Super Bowl with this core. Receiver is the team's biggest need. You can't rely on Samuel or Demarcus Robinson or rookie De'Zhaun Stribling , all coming off injuries, to get back to their preseason levels at this point. Go get a running mate for Evans and another weapon for Purdy, who has clearly been struggling to connect with his receivers as of late. The 49ers have had some struggles covering tight ends this year (Trey McBride, the Falcons group). Is there a concern that the Kirk Cousins to Brock Bowers combination could be a significant problem Sunday? Branch: The 49ers did allow their first two TDs to tight ends in the Week 7 loss in Atlanta, and McBride had nine catches for 75 yards in Week 3. Still, the presence of linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw is a big reason why the 49ers have actually been largely effective against tight ends: They are allowing six catches and 43.6 yards per game to the position. Like McBride, Bowers is good enough to inflate those numbers. He missed the first two regular-season games with a knee injury, but his per-game averages this season would translate to 116 catches for 1,550 yards and 14 TDs over 17 games. Killion: Sure it could be a problem. Cousins to Bowers will be defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' biggest concern. Bowers is the Raiders' biggest threat so he'll get a lot of attention and, like Harrison points out, the 49ers will be willing to see if someone else can beat them. It will be fun to see what Shanahan protege Klint Kubiak cooks up against his one-time mentor. Rich: The Cousins-to-Bowers connection is difficult for any opposing defense to contain. Cousins owns some of the best numbers among quarterbacks in 2026, and as Eric notes, Bowers has been on a tear. Bowers had two touchdowns last week against the Jets, and he reached the end zone in three of his prior five matchups. The 49ers might be best off doubling Bowers - or at least giving him extra attention - and forcing someone else to beat them. Prediction time. Who wins and why? Branch: Injuries will force the 49ers to trot out an underwhelming WR group for the second straight game after this crew's lack of production factored into their first loss of the season. The good news for the 49ers: They might be able to overwhelm the porous Raiders defense with Purdy, McCaffrey and Kittle doing nearly all the lifting. 49ers 27, Raiders 16 Killion: The 49ers got their bad loss out of the way two weeks ago, losing to Atlanta before the bye week, giving them a bad taste over their break. Now, they're rested and relaxed and ready for the final 10 games of the season. Shanahan is 6-1 after the bye week in the last seven years. 49ers 35, Raiders 20 Rich: A struggling 49ers offense against a struggling Raiders defense should make for an interesting matchup. Las Vegas has allowed at least 30 points in five straight weeks. The Rams put up 35 on them, and the Patriots scored 45. But this is a sneaky good offense led by Cousins. item.description: Shenendehowa celebrates after beating Saratoga in the Section 2, Class AAA finals on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - The Shenendehowa girls' volleyball team boasts a powerhouse up front, with several weapons the Mustangs can call on to make an impact. In Friday's Section 2 Class AAA championship, Shenendehowa's potent offense was the focus once again as the top-seeded Mustangs swept past No. 2 Saratoga Springs in straight sets 25-13, 25-14, 25-16, at Saratoga Springs High School. "It makes it so fun because the defense doesn't really have one person to focus on," Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. "They have to focus on three hitting options at all times, and running a 6-2 with two great setters, they're spreading it out. It's such a great part of our offense." Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped in five kills. Shenendehowa, the top-ranked team in the state Class AAA poll, pushed its sectional title win streak to six with. The four most recent championships have come in Class AAA since the state expanded to a six-classification system. "It's a completely new team than what we've had in the past," Ennist said. "It's a ton of younger girls and some seniors. It's just such a big mix and honestly, we're doing a great job together. It's so fun to be able to play with such a variety of ages and abilities out there." Key moment Shenendehowa trailed 6-5 in the second set, but used a pair of runs to gain control. The Mustangs used a 7-0 spurt to grab a 12-6 lead, and Ennist set up sophomore Leah Alfandre for a kill to cap a 5-1 run which provided Shenendehowa its first double-digit lead of the set, 17-7. "Those were really big for us, especially in a game this competitive," Ennist said. "If you do get into a little bit of a rut, you still have so much time to come out of it, and I think we did a really great job of getting that lead." Star of the game Shenendehowa freshman setter Kyli Kessler, the coach's daughter, turned in a stellar all-around performance. Kessler finished with 19 assists, 12 service points, including a pair of aces, and nine digs. "She works hard year-round on her game," Lori Kessler said of her daughter. item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Finds Home With Reds Or Nats
item.description: Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) is out on a batted ball during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power , but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees’ second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability. A Fresh Start in Washington The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm’s move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams. The Reds Need an Offensive Boost With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league’s lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm’s two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona’s order. The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. Under Aaron Boone, the Yankees made the postseason eight times over nine years, yet they must determine whether Chisholm belongs in their future. ESPN notes that free agents will come off the board quickly before the league shuts down on Dec. 1.

item.title: What Carlos Alcaraz said to Taylor Fritz after eliminating him from ATP Finals contention
item.description: Taylor Fritz had two match points on Carlos Alcaraz on Friday in his Paris Masters quarterfinal. He had taken the first set in a marathon tiebreaker and had all of the momentum leading 5-3 in the second set. Then, as if a light switch went off, Alcaraz raised his level and got the crowd involved. Fritz needed the win to qualify for the ATP Finasl, but 2 hours and 45 minutes later, it was not to be as Alcaraz won the match in three sets, 6-7, 7-5, 6-3. The quality of the tennis was high, but many were sad for Fritz who came so close to making the ATP Finals in a year where he battled a knee injury that kept him out of the game for some time. item.description: Sep 27, 2020; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) runs the ball against New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (97) during the first quarter of a NFL football game at MetLife Stadium. 49ers rumors: Brandon Aiyuk’s reinstatement chances ‘not promising’ in 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers boast one of the most recognizable NFL rosters from a names perspective and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who spoke to media on Friday , November 6, is certainly one of them. Christian McCaffrey and Nick Bosa are expected to be back for Week 9 , while the 2023 Second Team All-Pro receiver Aiyuk has been working to be reinstated to the NFL after a high profile parting of ways with the 49ers. Aiyuk hasn’t played since the 2024-25 NFL season. He suffered a serious knee injury and missed team meetings leading to the voiding of about $27 million of his contract and Aiyuk’s subsequent public trolling of the 49ers franchise. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN chimed in on the situation as Aiyuk and agent Drew Rosenhaus spoke to media. Fowler is not bullish on Aiyuk’s chances of being reinstated this season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Aiyuk wants to get reinstated to play in the NFL. His prospects in the short term are not promising, assuming he becomes a free agent eventually,” Fowler said. The 49ers are moving forward with a Brock Purdy-led passing game that has been beset by injuries lately. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel aren’t expected to play against the Raiders in Week 9. Purdy commented on the Aiyuk situation recently , painting the picture of a team that likes what it has in the locker room right now with little plans of changing much. Aiyuk has a long way to go toward restoring goodwill in the NFL, even with a huge body of work behind him in the league. He is one of the better receivers the 49ers have seen in the last decade, but it appears as if his time with GM John Lynch’s team is coming to a close. The New York Knicks have responded to Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride's recent comments about Taylor Swift that questioned her allegiance to the New York team. item.title: Ben James produces another low round and takes the 36-hole lead in Mexico
item.description: CABO SAN LUCAS, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 06: Ben James of the United States plays his shot from the fourth tee during the second round of the World Wide Technology Championship 2026 at El Cardonal at Diamante on November 06, 2026 in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images LOS CABOS, Mexico — Ben James ran off five straight birdies around the turn and finished with an aggressive tee shot for one last birdie and an 8-under 64 on Friday to build a one-shot lead going into the weekend at the World Wide Technology Championship. James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer. He already has four finishes in the top 5 and picking up plenty of experience along the way. A victory would put him on the Championship Series under the new model in 2028 and move him into the top 50 in the world. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” James was at 15-under 129 at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal at Diamante. He was one shot ahead of Peter Malnati, who was tied for the lead until coming up short of the green on the par-3 ninth and missing a 12-foot par putt to end his round of 64. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where ... I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair had a 68 and was three shots behind. This is the second time James has had the lead going into the weekend. The other was the RBC Canadian Open, and he shot a 78 to quickly spiral out of contention. He also had a good chance to win the Biltmore Championship Asheville until Jacob Bridgeman put on a putting clinic down the stretch in the final round. “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” He won the par-5 18th when he least expected it. James has been relying on his short wedges, and hit a pedestrian pitch to about 18 feet. But he holed the putt, and then started the front nine with three straight birdies to set the target. This is among the last three tournaments of the FedEx Cup Fall, after which the top 100 players keep full status for next year.

item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Decisive Statement on NFL Trade Deadline
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. The team must play a game–a pretty important game, really, as all these games are now made much more important thanks to recent failures–against the Colts on the road and, in doing so, they will see what a team in the midst of a massive sell looks like. The Colts have dumped stars in the past 10 days, and could dump at least one more if running back Jonathan Taylor is sent out by Tuesday. Might playing against a team in the throws of an on-the-fly rebuild inspire team owner Jerry Jones to shift his thinking and rebuild his spent draft capital? There has been ample conversation about trading away George Pickens, but that has apparently been more smoke than fire. But whether things could change was the question put to Jones on Friday afternoon during a radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, and the owner was clear in his stance. Cowboys ‘Commitment’ Won’t Change at NFL Trade Deadline Jones still thinks the 2026 Cowboys can be a good team. It’s an absurd thought based on the results so far, but maybe not so absurd when you consider the talent level on this team and the fact that the Cowboys are 3-5 and somehow still in a good position to win their otherwise terrible division. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tells @OThankKevin, @inthemageors and @AlecOnTheRadio that he's "a lot more likely" to add to the roster than sell at the trade deadline pic.twitter.com/eSshzPaZ9S— 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 6, 2026 Jones made that clear with his answer: “I have, I really believe that we have a team that the work we have done over the last 18 months, last year and this year, has real potential to play better than it’s played now. My situation, and I am not talking about Indianapolis, I am not talking about any other team, our situation, because the amount and the commitment and the changes we have made, it’s not the smart thing to do to make big adjustments. I would much more likely be adding to this direction than taking away from it.” The Cowboys will play the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Indianapolis. The NFL trade deadline follows on Tuesday, November 10. item.description: Denny Hamlin delivers a blunt assessment of his chances to win his first NASCAR Cup Series championship ahead of the season finale at Homestead-Miami. Getty Denny Hamlin enters Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway 70 points behind Kyle Larson and sees no realistic way to erase the gap. In fact, speaking at a press availability on Friday, Hamlin compared his chances to catch Larson and bring home the Cup to winning the lottery. “I mean, I don’t have any optimism. There’s obviously a chance you can win the lottery as well,” he said, sending a blunt message on where he believes he stands, as quoted by reporter Jeff Gluck. Hamlin has won 64 Cup races, more than all but eight drivers in NASCAR history. Yet somehow, he has never won a championship. His ‘don’t have any optimism’ remark followed Hamlin’s sixth-place finish at Martinsville Speedway on Nov. 1, where he called the title “unrealistic for sure,” as quoted by NASCAR.com after the race. He said the deficit to Larson needed to sit in the 40s to leave the No. 11 team with any degree of viable hope. He knocked down a three-pointer for the second consecutive game as well, and seems to have a stranglehold on the starting center spot for Ohio State for now.

item.title: ‘I’m The Real Champion’
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - MAY 09: Khamzat Chimaev of Russia prepares to face Sean Strickland in the UFC middleweight championship fight during the UFC 328 event at Prudential Center on May 09, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Khamzat Chimaev wants his UFC middleweight championship back and he’s willing to wait on the sidelines to get it. It’s been nearly six months since Chimaev suffered a massive upset loss at the hands of Sean Strickland at UFC 328, but the wound is still fresh. That’s because Chimaev was expected to handle Strickland in dominant fashion and start a 185-pound title reign that we haven’t seen since Israel Adesanya. Unfortunately for Chimaev, Strickland stifled his grappling efforts and ended up winning a decision to walk away with the undisputed UFC middleweight crown. Chimaev, who has been staying busy under the Real American Freestyle (RAF) banner , is steadfast on getting his title back and revenge on Strickland. The previously undefeated champion even stated that he’d follow Strickland all the way up to heavyweight in order to get a rematch. Some believe Chimaev had a bad training camp and weight cut for the first fight and that he’d right that wrong in another matchup with Strickland. The only problem is that Chimaev isn’t directly in line for another title shot. That belongs to red-hot contender Nassourdine Imavov, who is expected to fight Strickland in early 2027 if all things play out. Until then, Chimaev can only lobby for another shot at UFC’s 185-pound title and that’s exactly what he’s doing. The middleweight contender is willing to wait to fight the winner of Strickland and Imavov no matter how long it takes. It wouldn’t be a huge stretch for Chimaev heading into next year considering he hasn’t fought twice in one year since 2022. “I should fight the winner [of Strickland vs Imavov] because I’m the #1 contender,” said Chimaev in a recent interview with MMA Junkie . “I didn’t lose that match. I’m the real champion.”

Second, to (as much as possible) keep Allen contained in the pocket in those likely passing situations. If he buys himself time outside the pocket, more often than not you’re toast. Conversely, I’d be shocked if the Bills don’t test our shaky run defense early and often in this one to avoid those very scenarios. In addition, what makes the Bills’ offense so dangerous is their ability to convert 4th-and-short situations with Allen, who, at over 6’ 5” and nearly 240 pounds, is nearly impossible to stuff at the line of scrimmage. This can not only extend drives but also frustrate and demoralize a defense. If we’re to win this one, I can’t see us doing it without creating a turnover or two. The good news is that Allen does suffer from a bit of Stafforditis – i.e., elite QBs who are prone to throwing some head-scratching INTs. Hopefully, the pressure Flores will bring will help. James Cook has also had problems holding onto the ball this year, with four fumbles already, so there’s that, too. PREDICTION Wentz starting gives me a bit more confidence we can pull off the upset, but I can’t, in good conscience, pick the Vikings to win this game until I see something – anything – that resembles consistency from the offense. Scoring 24 points consistently shouldn’t be this difficult with our skill players. Wentz did make the most of the short fields the Packers gave us in Week 1, getting us to 39 points. Sure, there were TD drives of 1 play for 1 yard, 3 plays for 14 yards, and 6 plays for 28 yards. But we also had a 9-play, 83-yard scoring drive! It’s like the ‘98 Vikings and ‘99 Rams rolled into one! Holding Allen and the Bills offense under 20 in this game may require Flores to paint another masterpiece like the Week 17 game against the Lions last year at U.S. Bank Stadium. Can it happen? Absolutely. Will it happen? Ehhh, you can’t count on it. Regardless, it’d be nice not to have to rely on that every week, wouldn’t it? My guess: Wentz injects some much-needed life into the offense, but we come up short. Reverse psychology initiated. Buffalo Bills: 26 Minnesota Vikings: 24

item.title: Anthony Gordon Found Respect At Barcelona, Not Just In England
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - England Training - Swope Soccer Village, Kansas City, Missouri, U.S. - July 17, 2026 England's Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon during training IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jay Biggerstaff Anthony Gordon left the Premier League for Barcelona to get ‘respect,’ and he’s got it now . This summer, the 25-year-old English winger arrived from Newcastle United with an initial fee north of €70 million and instantly made an impact. He is already a key part of coach Hansi Flick’s attack alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha. It looks like he finally found the home he needed to really show his talent. Gordon never stopped believing he was meant for the top level, even through the hard times. His boyhood club Everton saw him fight relegation, while a 2021 loan spell took him to Preston North End. He also dealt with scoreless streaks after moving to Newcastle in 2023. But he never lost faith in his own ability to succeed at the highest level. A System That Fits His Style Earlier this season, Gordon spoke about people in England starting to respect ” the quality and IQ that I play with .” His comments were seen as a sign he had not always gotten the recognition he deserved back home. He told ESPN that he did not mean that people were judging him unfairly or that they had a negative view of him. He simply meant they had never seen him in a system that highlights these qualities before. People hadn’t seen him in this kind of system before, which he thinks is helping them appreciate him more. The move to Spain seems to have unlocked a side of his game that the Premier League could not show. Maxime Estève, a defender now at RB Leipzig, told ESPN that Gordon is really good and sharp with a great right foot. Estève said Gordon is great at one-on-ones and wants to beat the right back every time. Was Leaving England Necessary? Was departing the Premier League necessary for him to achieve this? It seems the answer is yes for Gordon. The English game often demands a certain type of physical play that can hide a player’s true brain and skill set. Barcelona offers a different kind of football that lets his IQ shine through on the field. Now a regular starter, he kicked off Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League victory over Aston Villa. Gordon and Barcelona will kick off their LaLiga clash against Atlético Madrid this Sunday at the top of the table. The fans in England might have missed out on seeing his full potential for a few more years. Now they get to watch him thrive on one of the biggest stages in world soccer. The respect he wanted is now being given to him in spades by the Spanish league.

item.title: San Francisco 49ers Announce Christian McCaffrey Decision Before Raiders Game
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are 6-1 entering Week 9 of the NFL season as they prepare to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Following Friday’s practice, the team provided several key injury updates and officially ruled out veteran wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, leaving the 49ers offense quite shorthanded. However, they also received positive injury news on star running back Christian McCaffrey, who sustained a mild hamstring injury the last time San Francisco took the field in Week 7. McCaffrey Off Injury Report vs. Raiders In positive news, McCaffrey will be good to go for Sunday’s contest after the 49ers officially removed him from the injury report. He logged back-to-back practices on Thursday and Friday. McCaffrey has played in every game this season and continues to serve as a workhorse in Kyle Shanahan’s high-powered offense. He’ll likely have to shoulder an even greater workload this week with the WR corps so depleted. Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will play Week 9. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 6, 2026 Earlier this week, McCaffrey revealed that he was caught off guard when he learned the injury was a hamstring issue, but said he “feels great.” “I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury],” McCaffrey said Wednesday. “Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you… It wasn’t too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great.” McCaffrey’s 2026 Season With 49ers McCaffrey has appeared in all seven games, recording 84 carries for 389 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. He’s also caught 34 passes for 251 yards. He’s in his 11th NFL season and fifth with the 49ers after San Francisco acquired him from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 in exchange for four draft picks. 49ers Welcoming Back Nick Bosa Another positive sign for the 49ers is that they’ll welcome back star pass rusher Nick Bosa, who has missed several games this season with a calf strain he sustained during practice. Bosa will line up alongside DeForest Buckner, who will make his first start with the 49ers since San Francisco acquired him from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye week. He still has work to do with his hand placement, but Seaton has improved in his polish, eye awareness and overall technique, especially in pass protection. Seaton has the twitch and size to be a valid blindside protector at the next level. 5. Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State Much will be made about Mestemaker’s lack of experience as a starting quarterback at any level (he was a backup in high school and then a walk-on at North Texas). Despite not having the experience or snaps that other typically highly touted quarterbacks have, Mestemaker seems to know how to play the position. He has a good arm that can access all parts of the field and is willing to push the ball from muddy pockets. He can change arm slots and layer the football up and over defenders when needed. Mestemaker is tall and has a long frame that he has started to fill out. He is a solid athlete, albeit not an overwhelming one. But he has a loose arm, is very good at avoiding sacks despite his lack of experience, and can consistently throw on the move, even when working left. Mestemaker is willing to move and work from the pocket and has enough giddyup to work outside of it, too. He has had some inconsistent performances the past few weeks with his decision-making, plays in a very conducive offense that can make his eyes lock in a bit too much (he has yet to take an under-center snap, not a damning thing but worth noting), and hasn’t played the toughest competition so far this season. But Mestemaker has the ability to create throws within and out of structure, and has the size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) and enough arm to translate to the next level. (Joseph Raines/Yahoo Sports) 6. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas Simmons is an explosive athlete who is asked to do everything for Texas’ defense. He has shined while pinning his ears back and getting after the passer. He wins with a quick first step and has the ability to run the hoop and turn a corner on offensive tackles. He has been asked to drop into coverage in his college career, and also mirror athletic quarterbacks on passing downs, showing off the front-seven versatility modern defenses love. Simmons’ agility and speed shine in these other areas. 7. Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana An outside receiver with size (6-foot-4, 208 pounds) and long speed, Becker burst onto the scene in a talented wide receiver room and was constantly coming down with big catches in big moments. Becker has strong hands and excellent hand-eye coordination in catching range that allows him to frequently come down with the football. He has long legs, but also shows enough quickness and bend to run a fully developed route tree, which raises his ceiling. 8. Arch Manning, QB, Texas Manning’s 2026 season has been a journey of ups and downs . He still displays the size (6-foot-4, 222 pounds), athleticism, pocket movement and willingness to push the ball that make for an intriguing prospect. That willingness to push the ball, even in too-often mucky pockets, leads to exciting plays but also game-swinging negative ones, too. Manning’s results haven’t always set the world on fire, but he has a style that translates to the next level, namely that aggression and lack of fear throwing into tight windows or tight pockets. When grouped with his speed and arm, he makes for a still-intriguing package at quarterback. More consistent results will help it all feel better. Manning still has to learn to take an easier answer quicker, which to me is to use his legs and rushing ability more often, something he’s tapped back into in recent weeks. His process, while far from perfect, is cleaner when reviewing it on film, especially amid a frustrating Texas offensive ecosystem. 9. Zereoue Williams, OT, Utah Williams is an easy-moving athlete who gets better each week. This former basketball player is an older prospect, but he is still tapping into his potential because of his relative lack of experience at the position and football altogether. He has twitchiness, foot speed and length to develop into a longtime blindside protector. There is also enough strength to be an asset in the run game. 10. Chris Cole, LB, Georgia Cole has sideline-to-sideline range, which isn’t hyperbolic as he actually displays it. He plays with his hair on fire, has the range to cover large swaths of the middle of the field, and shows an ability to come forward in the run game and as a blitzer. Cole’s versatility and four-down ability is what a modern linebacker looks like. 11. Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson Hampton is a big and long corner who can play in zone and impact the game with his size (6-foot-2, 205 pounds) and awareness, but might actually be most unlocked as a player in man coverage situations. He is not overly twitchy, yet he’s a smooth athlete who can fluidly get in and out of his turns. His size, foot speed and ball skills give him a chance at being a lockdown player on the outside at the next level. He reminds me a bit of James Bradberry. 12. I have kept his ranking and report as is. Si

item.title: Former Dodgers Hitting Coach Aaron Bates Explains Why He Left
item.description: Former Los Angeles Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates opened up about the behind-the-scenes details of his departure. After 12 years with the Dodgers, Bates is moving on after contract negotiations stalled. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) How Aaron Bates and the Dodgers parted ways According to Bates, he received a multi-year offer, which he told Maddie Lee of the LA Times was “not a competitive offer.” He rejected the offer and expected talks to continue, but no other follow-up offer came. “Basically, they said, ‘I think we should go our separate ways,” Bates told The LA Times. “I was just very taken aback, in a sense, by that.” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes did not comment on the talks, but told The Times that he wished “nothing but the best for Bates and his family.” Sep 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes during the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Reflecting on how things played out, Bates didn’t seem to hold any bitter feelings about how it worked out. “Processing it, I think that there’s always a time and a place, and I think that things run their course,” Bates said to Lee. “But I have nothing but amazing things to say about the Dodgers organization and people. “My kids grew up Dodgers, and I grew up a Dodger, as a coach. It’s just unfortunate the way it’s worked out towards these last few days.” Feb 20, 2019; Glendale, AZ, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers assistant hitting coach Aaron Bates poses for a portrait during media day at Camelback Ranch. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) What is next for Aaron Bates and the Dodgers? With experience in a highly esteemed organization like the Dodgers and as a three-time champion, Bates should land on his feet easily. In fact, he told the Times that he is already speaking with other teams. “I’m talking to many different teams, and we’re kind of working through some things, and I’ll leave it at that for now,” he said. “But it’s exciting times in that sense.” Regarding the Dodgers, they will likely now either promote internally or bring in someone from another organization, but either way, there will be a fresh voice on the coaching staff. Changes on successful teams can be tough, but after a disappointing NLCS exit in which the offense went cold, shaking things up could help.

item.title: Broncos Roster Move Spells Excellent Sign for Talanoa Hufanga
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Talanoa Hufanga #9 of the Denver Broncos during warm up before the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty The Denver Broncos made what some consider to be a surprise move when they released safety Taylor Rapp on Friday. Despite starting the season on the practice squad, Rapp played a starting role on defense over the past three weeks, and prior to his third start in Week 8, was elevated to the active roster. Now no longer having need of the 28-year old’s services implies that safety Talanoa Hufanga; who did not practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday; is good to go for Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Mild surprise! A good sign that Hufanga is good to go for Sunday tho. https://t.co/l8De2L6wIJ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 6, 2026 Taylor Rapp Cut; Suggests Talanoa Hufanga Will Play Week 9 The former Buffalo Bill had been covering Hufanga’s duties whilst the two-time All-Pro safety dealt with an ankle injury over the past few weeks, alongside fellow starter Brandon Jones . Officially, Hufanga is “questionable”, but the timing of the announcement feels inescapable; the Broncos surely would not release their interim starter for the past three weeks without a high degree of confidence that their top guy was ready to go. Especially given the two next men up, Devon Key and Tycen Anderson , have four combined NFL starts between them. Even then, two of Key’s starts were in Week 6 and Week 7, during which he played less than 40% of snaps on defense, with Rapp and Jones seeing the majority of the action. Anderson himself is mostly a special teams contributor, so if Hufanga is not ready, then the Broncos will have no full-time safety option behind Jones and Key. item.title: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season
item.description: HOLLAND - The Hope College women's basketball team has been a national powerhouse for decades. Designed to win with defense, this year's version of the Flying Dutch has two experienced point guards leading the way on both sides of the ball. Starting point guard Terin Maynard pushes the pace, drives to the basket and anchors the perimeter defense. While most teams lose quite a bit when a backup point guard goes in. For Hope, there is hardly a noticeable difference when Josie DeSmit checks in. The duo led Hope to a 72-65 win over Wisconsin-Platteville on Friday, Nov. 6, at DeVos Fieldhouse to open the season - both scoring career highs in the process. More: Hope College women's basketball reloads 2026-27 roster after run to Sweet 16 Maynard scored a career-high 20 points to go along with six assists, while DeSmit had a career-high 15 points with three steals. Leah Richards had 15 points and eight rebounds. "They were really good today," Hope coach Brian Morehouse said. "Josie is good enough to start and played her role very well. It gives us a two-headed monster and that is really hard on other teams." The game was close in the fourth quarter and Morehouse chose to play both point guards together. DeSmit nailed a 3-pointer, then scored another basket to make it 64-54 with 4:50 to go. "We showed our resilience and found a way to stick together and do the dirty work," Maynard said. The Pioneers closed the gap again and Maynard took over with three-point play and a basket in the paint to make it 71-63 with 2:26 to go. "We withstood 11 from 3 and gutted it out. We switched our defenses up and our defense was really good, but they had a lot of good shots in the last seconds of the shot clock. We played both of them together and if they can rebound a little more we will see that some more." It was a fun change. "We push each other every day in practice. I get to go up against the best defender in the MIAA. We feed off each other well and have some good chemistry," DeSmit said. "We both have our own strengths. Those differences help a ton on the court." This is the second year they have been the top two point guards on the roster. "It has been awesome to have her. When we do both go out there, we have the confidence in each other and can read each other," Maynard said. "We found a way to do that well." It could key another strong season for the Flying Dutch. "We have a lot of potential this year," Maynard said. "We have great new freshman who have grown our circle and we are starting better than we finished last year. We can only go up." item.title: Claudio Castagnoli Calls League of Legends ‘the Best Sport to Watch’
item.description: Pro Wrestler for AEW Claudio Castagnoli makes an announcement at League of Legends Worlds 2026 QuarterFinals Day 4 on Friday, November 06, 2026 in Allen, Texas. ALLEN, Texas — Finding new hobbies can be difficult, especially when you’re on the road for 300-plus days a year. Pro wrestler Claudio Castagnoli has always liked gaming. Still, he didn’t start playing League of Legends until a showmatch crossover between his former company (WWE) and Riot Games introduced him to it. It’s been eight years since that showmatch, and a lot has changed. He works for a new company (All Elite Wrestling) and doesn’t have enough time to play as many games as he’d like. But he still finds time to watch League of Legends, including stopping by the World Championship quarterfinal match between Korea’s T1 and France’s Karmine Corp. “League of Legends is the best sport to watch,” he said. “It’s so exciting.” Castagnoli appeared on the live broadcast, where he announced the teams as they entered the arena and was also interviewed. For him, the chance to see the League of Legends World Championships is too good to pass up. Despite his world travels this year, including Mexico, the United Kingdom, and Japan, he hasn’t been to Korea to soak up the heart of esports. “I’m sure [League of Legends is] kind of popular over there,” Castagnoli said with a smirk. He compared the League of Legends crowd at the event to the rabid fans who attend AEW shows. He’s been to a League of Legends event in China and said the experience is similar to the events he works. “It’s the passion of the fans for the team, for the game, and how they show it,” Castagnoli said. “They have signs. They come early. They dress up. They wear jerseys. They show their passion and pride.” More importantly, he compared the title and pro wrestling as two industries that have immense lore and histories that fans can track for years. Take weekly AEW television and the stories that advance week to week, and compare it to traditional media such as Arcane . Both build character lore and offer ways to attract fans while providing more content. The thing, however, he said that was also similar was the idea that all it takes is exposure to the game and environment to get people hooked. “There are a lot of people that are like, ‘I’m not really into it,’” Castagnoli said. “I’m like, ‘Well, if you come to a live show, you’ll be a fan just because you see it.’ Once you play, and I feel like, especially once you play with your friends, it just becomes so much more fun because we can all watch Worlds at the highest level.” He also offered advice to new League of Legends fans. “Don’t try to imitate because it’s quite frustrating,” Castagnoli said. While Castagnoli can make physical feats seem effortless, such as his trademark giant swing, micro movements with a mouse and maneuvering around the Rift (the name of League of Legends’ map) offer a different challenge. “I’m the worst. I misclick and click the wrong buttons,” he said.

item.title: Matthias Jaissle caught in the storm as Newcastle struggle without European fix
item.description: Panic building among fans as club visit Craven Cottage but head coach has resolute support of hierarchy At least Matthias Jaissle has a sense of humour. “There’s a lot of storm at the moment,” reflected Newcastle’s head coach on Thursday. A wry smile suggested he was not referring to the north-east weather. Jaissle has seen his tactics, team selection, man management and entire philosophy rubbished in recent days but, on current evidence, appears to be holding his nerve. After all, it is not Jaissle’s fault that his appointment has coincided with supporters, players and directors struggling to adjust to life without Champions League involvement. A disappointing 12th-place finish under Eddie Howe last season dictates that there are no more exciting trips to Barcelona, Paris and Marseille and, significantly, no much-needed boost to club finances. Indeed, Newcastle are finding life without last term’s continental fix so tricky that they travel to Fulham on Saturday with the disgruntled mindset of a passenger accustomed to flying business class who suddenly finds themselves stuck in a cramped, mid-row economy seat. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
item.description: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27. The former are one of only five teams in the history of the English top flight to have failed to score in their first four home league matches. Three of the preceding four also drew a blank in game five, which will be deflating news for Oliver Glasner with Manchester City heading to the City Ground on Saturday looking for a win after consecutive league defeats. Forest’s expected goals total implies they should have scored but a flaw in their data shows a reason why. They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
